answer.explanation: Beacon production (lumen/prod) keeps web sessions in Redis. The rationale says this was approved because sessions must survive a web server restart. The accountable owner today is Eli Varga.

Beacon production keeps web sessions in Redis. The approved architecture decision says this is because sessions must survive a web server restart. Dee Laine owns that decision, and the governance charter shows Dee is the authorized approver for production/staging architecture.

Beacon staging currently uses the Redis session store decision D4, effective in staging by 2026-10-15. The rationale says sessions are stored in Redis in production and staging, and the owner resolution for D4 at this date is Eli Varga.

The Beacon staging session store is currently owned by Dee Laine. The applicable approved decision is D4, which says sessions are stored in Redis in both production and staging and is explicitly approved and owned by Dee Laine. P08 shows Dee Laine is authorized to approve architecture for staging, so this authority applies here.

On 2026-07-01, the applicable production session-store decision for Beacon/Lumen is D4, 'Redis session store.' It is supported by ADR-4 and approved/owned by Dee Laine; the governance charter shows Dee approves Lumen production architecture decisions.
On 2026-07-01, the Beacon production session store decision is D4: sessions are stored in Redis in production, and it is approved and owned by Dee Laine.

Harbor staging users sign in with passkeys now. Decision D8 applies to harbor/staging as of 2026-10-15, and it replaces the earlier staging-only OIDC sign-in decision. The supporting rationale says this was approved to trial phishing-resistant login and is owned by Ana Ruiz.

Harbor staging users now sign in with passkeys. The currently applicable decision is ADR-6 (D8), which from 2026-06-01 replaces ADR-3 for staging only and says staging uses passkeys to trial phishing-resistant login. Ana Ruiz owns and approved that decision, and the governance charter says Ana Ruiz approves architecture decisions for Harbor production and staging.
Harbor production users sign in with company single sign-on (OIDC). The currently applicable decision for production is D3, effective 2025-02-01, and it is owned by Ana Ruiz.
Harbor production users sign in through company single sign-on (OIDC). This is the approved production decision effective since 2025-02-01, and it is owned by Ana Ruiz.

Harbor production currently exports customer data via the approved nightly batch export decision D2, which is effective in production from 2025-06-01. D2 replaced the earlier real-time export choice D1 after the INC-42 postmortem showed real-time export saturated the production database and delayed checkout; the change was approved by ben, who remains the accountable owner.

Harbor production exports customer data in a nightly batch today because ADR-2 is the approved production decision effective 2025-06-01, and it explicitly replaces ADR-1 for production only. Ben Okafor owns that decision. The stated rationale is that the real-time export saturated the production database at peak load and delayed checkout for 40 minutes; a nightly batch removes the peak.

On 2027-03-01, Harbor production exports customer data hourly. That choice is set by decision D9, which replaced the earlier nightly batch export for production. The accountable owner is Ben Okafor (ben).

On 2027-03-01, Harbor production exports customer data hourly. ADR-7 (D9), effective 2027-02-01 and approved by authorized approver Ben Okafor, replaces ADR-2 for production only. ADR-2 had previously replaced real-time exports in production. The ownership of the current choice is Ben Okafor.

Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The applicable decision is D1 for harbor/staging at 2026-10-15, and its rationale states that Harbor exports customer data in real time in production and staging. Ownership is Ana Ruiz / ana.

Harbor staging exports customer data in real time today. The approved decision is ADR-1 (D1), which applies to both production and staging and says Harbor exports customer data in real time because partner dashboards need fresh data. Ana Ruiz is the authorized approver and owner for this architecture decision in staging.

Beacon production currently releases daily behind feature flags. This is supported by decision D7, which is applicable in production as of 2026-10-15 and supersedes the earlier weekly-release decision D6. The accountable owner is Fay Osei.

Beacon production releases daily behind feature flags as of 2026-05-01. The approved decision is D7, and the release-process authority for production is Fay Osei; the charter update says Eli no longer approves this area while Fay continues to.

I could not find a supported decision that answers how often Beacon staging releases. The only applicable decision returned for staging is about Redis session storage, while a release-frequency decision was set aside and therefore does not currently apply.

I found a staging release note saying Beacon staging releases on every merge, but the approver is not authorized for staging, so I can't treat it as an approved current decision. I did not find another supported authorized decision for staging release frequency.

Beacon production (lumen/prod) will keep web sessions in Memcached on 2027-01-15. The currently applicable approved decision is D5, effective 2026-12-01, which replaces the earlier Redis session store for production only. Owner: Dee Laine.

On 2027-01-15, Beacon production keeps web sessions in Memcached. The applicable approved decision is D5, effective 2026-12-01, which replaces ADR-4 for production only. D5 is approved and owned by Dee Laine, and the governance charter confirms Dee approves architecture for Lumen/Beacon production and staging.

Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The applicable decision on 2027-03-01 for harbor/staging is D1, and its rationale says Harbor exports customer data in real time in production and staging because partner dashboards need fresh data. The accountable owner is Ana Ruiz (ana).

On 2027-03-01, Harbor staging exports customer data in real time. The governing decision is ADR-1, which applies to both production and staging and was approved by an authorized approver; it is owned by Ana Ruiz. A later incident note mentions a nightly batch removing peak load, but it is not an approved decision and does not override ADR-1.
On 2026-03-01, Beacon production (Lumen/prod) releases once a week, specifically on Tuesday. The approved decision is D6, and the accountable owner is Eli Varga (eli).
Beacon production releases once a week on Tuesday. This decision is approved and owned by Eli Varga.
